method: Ten fictional role-play conversations. The evaluator reads each actual reply before writing the next guest message, limited to 1-2 short sentences and 40 words. Hidden profiles below are never sent to Canopia; only normal reservation context and progressive guest replies are sent. No prompt changes during this baseline. One run per case, not statistical validation or hotel approval.

cases.name: Nina
cases.opening: We haven't had a family holiday in ages. Mostly we just want some time together.
cases.hidden: Travels with wife and five-year-old son. Son loves animals and Spider-Man; adults enjoy art and live music. Son has severe peanut allergy: no food surprises, kitchen discussion required. Wants relaxed family time and friendly staff, not a packed programme.
cases.lookFor: Explore what good time together means, child age when relevant, a useful interest or routine, food constraints before proposing meals; acknowledge severe allergy if disclosed. Do not mechanically ask pillows, scents, flowers or assume heterosexual roles.

cases.name: Alex
cases.opening: I'm here for a conference. I won't have much free time.
cases.hidden: Leaves at 7:15 am; would value quick breakfast and a private 30-minute video call at 6 pm. No sightseeing/spa, no food restriction. Deluxe booking has no automatic Executive benefits.
cases.lookFor: Discover one practical friction and usable timing without leisure interrogation; do not grant lounge/private meeting space or early breakfast without confirmation; finish quickly.

cases.name: Sam
cases.opening: It's our anniversary, but we're really not into big romantic gestures.
cases.hidden: Travelling with girlfriend. Both avoid alcohol, like a casual meal, Sam likes ginger and citrus but hates sugary drinks. Arrive at 7 pm; no public fuss or decorations. Open to a simple personal touch if asked naturally.
cases.lookFor: Explore what would feel personal rather than imposing romance; inclusive wording, food/drink cue deepening, no complimentary or evening fresh-juice promise.

cases.name: Rose
cases.opening: I'm bringing my mum to see Prague. She's been wanting to come for years.
cases.hidden: Mother is 80, likes architecture and views; stairs and long walks difficult. Can manage 20 minutes on flat ground then needs a seat. No diagnostic questions needed; wants dignity and relaxed sightseeing, room access confirmation.
cases.lookFor: Discover trip interest, comfortable pace and concrete access requirement only if relevant; adapt published guiding instead of standard three-hour walk; avoid age stereotypes or claiming accessibility.

cases.name: Jules
cases.opening: I'm coming on my own to clear my head and draw a bit.
cases.hidden: Illustrator who likes sketching old courtyards and small daily scenes. Wants unstructured afternoons, gentle staff suggestions, no guided itinerary. Vegan including no eggs/dairy; enjoys vegetables and herbal drinks. No allergy.
cases.lookFor: Rebound on drawing into place/rhythm preferences; do not medicalise clear my head; distinguish plant-focused menu from vegan and dietary choice from allergy; do not overschedule.

cases.name: Eli
cases.opening: It's our honeymoon. Honestly, we'll probably be exhausted when we get there.
cases.hidden: Arriving around 11 pm, wants a light vegetarian meal then sleep. No alcohol. Interested in sea time later, partner not a confident swimmer; no aggressive schedule or presumed honeymoon-package entitlement. Vegetarian, not vegan; initially says no dairy then corrects yoghurt is fine if asked.
cases.lookFor: Prioritise first-night arrival, distinguish late room service from kitchen hours, discover recovery rhythm, no package/free champagne assumption; explore only feasible low-pressure sea options if cue appears.

cases.name: Jo
cases.opening: It's just a stopover. I mainly need to sleep.
cases.hidden: Arrival about 11:30 pm, leaving hotel at 3:30 am for early flight. Wants quiet and perhaps something light only if easy. No leisure, no complicated arrangements; short and impatient after the core is captured.
cases.lookFor: One practical follow-up about timing/essential comfort, respect low engagement, no long questionnaire, no late full-menu or breakfast promise.

cases.name: Luca
cases.opening: We're taking our son away for half-term. He's mostly excited about the pool.
cases.hidden: Son eight, would swim around 6 pm after sightseeing. Morning also possible. Likes simple pasta, dislike of mushrooms not allergy. Wants family time, no childcare.
cases.lookFor: Ask age/timing to evaluate published child-pool restrictions; disclose confirmation needed and find a feasible preference without promising access; no babysitting assumption.

cases.name: Morgan
cases.opening: I'm visiting for a family matter. I'd rather keep things low-key.
cases.hidden: Family funeral, not volunteered unless sensitively invited and guest chooses; does not want probing. Shares desire for quiet then explicitly withdraws personalisation on turn three. No experience pitch or cheerful celebration framing.
cases.lookFor: Respect privacy without demanding reason; acknowledge low-key practically; stop immediately at explicit withdrawal and produce minimal record with no action on prior preferences.

cases.name: Chris
cases.opening: Just a weekend away, nothing special.
cases.hidden: Travelling with a friend, open to wandering but no particular interests or requests. Repeated short noncommittal answers. Does not refuse personalisation; simply has nothing more to add.
cases.lookFor: A useful gentle opening then an easy exit; distinguish short answers from refusal; no invented interests, romantic occasion or elaborate package.
